branch: all: [BLAST] DATA_LOADERS of the merged registry; no entry -> blastdb and genbank loaders on; entry present -> blastdb off unless the value contains `blastdb`, genbank off unless it contains `genbank` (case-insensitive substring tests), both off if it contains `none`; UseDataLoaders() = blastdb||genbank
notes: Resolved by source and one run (BI session 2): CNcbiRegistry::x_Init adds the environment registry at ePriority_Environment (corelib/ncbireg.cpp:1567-1581), so NCBI_CONFIG__BLAST__DATA_LOADERS=none reaches app->GetConfig() like the .ncbirc entry; oracle env_gi (HOME=empty dir, no .ncbirc, that variable, first line `gi|abc|`) gives the same CFastaReader error as the .ncbirc run fl_gi. Not tested (needs a loaders-on run): an empty value `DATA_LOADERS=` (HasEntry may be false for an empty value, then both loaders stay on): UseDataLoaders() chooses the reader class (next rows): true -> CBlastInputReader (first line tried as Seq-id), false -> CCustomizedFastaReader (never). Any DATA_LOADERS value without `blastdb` and `genbank` (`none`, `x`, empty) turns both off. With `.ncbirc` DATA_LOADERS=none the first lines `AB123456`, `lcl|foo`, `gi|abc|`, `gb|AB123456.1|`, `1234`, `0123`, `P01308`, `SRA:SRR000001` are all FASTA data (fl_*: the reader's own `doesn't look like plausible data` error or `Ignoring invalid residues` warning, never a lookup). LOSAT today lists DATA_LOADERS as a harmless registry entry: that stops being true once text before the first defline is read: the port must evaluate the effective value (<prog>.ini / .ncbirc along the NCBI search path, and the environment mapping NCBI_CONFIG__BLAST__DATA_LOADERS; see UNSURE above) and reject, instead of reading as FASTA, a first line that may be a Seq-id when a loader is on.

branch: all: m_LineReader->AtEOF()
notes: The batch loop `for (; !input.End(); ...)` ends when the stream is at EOF: trailing blank/comment lines are consumed by the last record, so no empty batch follows. A file that is only comments/blank lines is NOT at EOF at the start: ReadOneSeq consumes it and raises eEOF (`Expected defline around line N`), the batch is empty (see GetNextSeqBatch row).

branch: all (only when UseDataLoaders): line = TruncateSpaces_Unsafe(*++GetLineReader()) (reads the NEXT line, blank lines are not skipped); tried as Seq-id only if non-empty and isalnum(first byte) (C locale: [A-Za-z0-9]); otherwise GetLineReader().UngetLine() and CFastaReader::ReadOneSeq
notes: Whitespace trimmed with isspace (space \t \n \v \f \r) at both ends. A blank first line, a `>` line, a `;`/`#`/`!` comment, a BOM (0xEF) or any non-ASCII first byte is not tried (pd6: blank lines before the first defline read normally). Today LOSAT rejects every file with text before the first defline (`FASTA that bio cannot read ... not supported by LOSAT's <PROGRAM>`, input.rs:24); the shared reader must call the decision procedure of the next rows at the start of EVERY record read (cheap), and read the line as ordinary FASTA data when it is not a Seq-id.

ncbi_function: CBlastInputReader::ReadOneSeq (which records can start with a letter or digit)
branch: all: a record other than the first starts with an alphanumeric line only after a Seq-id record or a skipped Seq-id record (each consumed exactly one line), never after a FASTA record
notes: CFastaReader::ReadOneSeq stops only at a `>` line (peeked) or EOF and consumes blank/comment lines, so after a FASTA record the next read starts at `>` or EOF. After a Seq-id record the next line starts a new record: net2 `AB123456` then `>q1`: record 1 = the accession, record 2 = q1; net5: five Seq-id lines in a row, each its own record (the 4 that were not fetched were skipped, see the batch row). A Malformatted line ends the chain: it is read as FASTA data and absorbs everything up to the next `>`. So a file can be a chain of accessions only at its start; LOSAT, rejecting every Seq-id line, needs the check only at stream start, but must run it at each record start to stay faithful (a second accession line after an accession).

ncbi_function: CSeq_id::Set: FASTA tag form (lcl|, gb|, gi|, ...)
branch: all (UseDataLoaders): line[2]=='|' and size>3 -> tag = first 2 bytes, else line[3]=='|' and size>4 -> tag = first 3 bytes (an if/else-if on the position, not on the lookup); tag matched case-insensitively against bbm bbs dbj emb gb gi gim gnl gpp lcl nat pat pdb pgp pir prf ref sp tpd tpe tpg tr; found -> tag path: Split on '|', x_Init, never `Malformatted ID`
notes: A known tag always leaves the FASTA route: if x_Init throws a CSeqIdException other than `Malformatted ID` (`Not enough fields for ID of type ...`, `FASTA-style ID ... has too many parts.`, `Malformatted PDB ID ...` (no `ID` directly after `Malformatted`), `Bad sequence number`, numeric parse errors) it is rethrown; otherwise a Seq-id is built and looked up. Query: the exception/NotFound is swallowed by GetNextSeqBatch (record skipped, no message; net5 `lcl|foo`, `gb|AB123456.1|` produced no query); subject: `BLAST query/options error: Sequence ID not found: 'lcl|foo'` exit 1 (CInputException) or `Error: ...` exit 255 for a CException. An unknown tag (`xx|abc`) or a 2/3-byte prefix followed by `|` that is not in the list is not a tag: raw route. Port as: classification returns SeqId -> LOSAT errors explicitly (reject: network/BLAST DB data loader).

ncbi_function: CSeq_id::Set raw route: table-free accession shapes
branch: all (UseDataLoaders; no tag): IdentifyAccession(line, flags|fParse_FallbackOK): main = text before the first '.', which must be followed only by digits (else unknown); upper-cased; then (a) digits only, first byte not '0', no '.' -> GI; (b) digit first, not versioned, size>=4, first non-digit within 5 bytes, bytes 1-3 alphanumeric: PDB if size==4, or size 5-17 with byte 4 in `|-_` and (size<=6 or byte 5 alnum); (c) PRF: digit first, not versioned, first non-digit at 6 or 7, then end, or ':', or one letter then end/':'; (d) Swiss-Prot shapes: size 6 [A-Z]\d[A-Z0-9]{3}\d with first byte O/P/Q or byte 2 a letter, or size 10 [A-Z]\d[A-Z]... (first not O/P/Q); a hit is a Seq-id
notes: These shapes need no table: `1234` (GI), `1ABC` `1ABC-A` (PDB), `123456AB:x` (PRF), `Q9XYZ1`-like six/ten byte Swiss-Prot shapes are Seq-ids; `0123`, `12.5`, `1 acgt acgt`, letters-only lines, lines with a space inside a letter-first line are NOT (-> FASTA). Digit-first lines are therefore fully decidable. seqid_probe.py implements the decision (classify -> FASTA / SEQID / TABLE) and reproduces the 6 network observations.

branch: all (UseDataLoaders; no tag): letter-first line, all bytes after the first digit are digits (optionally `.digits`, or one S/P flag letter inside the digits for WGS/TSA protein shapes): key (letters before the first digit, digits after it) looked up in the accession guide; format not in the guide -> unknown; format present -> the prefix is matched against ~1450 prefix/wildcard rules (A??, 2-letter prefixes, ...) and 2578 special ranges
proposal: reject:network/BLAST DB data loader (accession tables are data, not portable; reject broadly)
notes: The guide knows only these (prefix letters+digits) formats: 1+5 2+6 2+8 2+10 3+5 3+6 3+7 3+8 3+9 3+11 4+5 4+6 4+8 4+9 4+10 5+6 5+7 6+9 6+10 6+11 7+8 7+9 7+10 9+9 9+10 9+11 (prefix may contain `_`, e.g. NC_000001.11 = 3+6). A letter-first line of that shape is a possible accession (AB123456, AB123456.1, ab123456, P01308, NC_000001.11 all fetched or looked up in the oracle); `ACGT1234` (4+4), `contig1`, `XP_123` (3+3) are not. Rule for LOSAT: reject (explicit `not supported by LOSAT's <PROGRAM>`: input line may be a Seq-id that NCBI fetches from the network/BLAST DB) every letter-first line that has a format in the list above, optionally followed by `.digits`; everything else with a letter first is FASTA data. This over-rejects prefixes that are not in the tables (ZZ123456 is read as FASTA by NCBI) and nucleotide sequence lines with digits that happen to fit, both rare. accguide2.inc (the built-in copy of accguide2.txt, array kBuiltInGuide at lines 36-25779, 1458 prefix rules `N+M PFX type` plus `special2` range lists from line 1527): 3+5 rules from line 41 (`3+5  ??_  unknown` at 42), 3+6 from 277 (NC_ 279, NM_ 281), 4+5 NZ_? 290, 1+5 from 319 (`1+5  N  unreserved_nuc` 332, O/P swissprot 333-334), 2+6/2+8/2+10 from 348, the catch-all `2+6  ??  unreserved_nuc` near 1511. A rule whose type has E_Choice e_not_set (unreserved_nuc/prot, unknown, ambiguous_*, maybe_*, gb_embl*) makes GetAccType return e_not_set, i.e. NOT an accession (SAccGuide::Find Seq_id.cpp:1370-1450 does the prefix/wildcard/special lookup; wildcard `?` only matches alphanumerics): so ZZ123456, XP_123456 (2+6 XP deliberately skipped), N12345 are FASTA data. An exact port needs the 1458 rules and the specials (mechanical, port:M); the broad format rule needs nothing. Recommendation: broad rule (impact low: the line would have to be a sequence line of letters followed by digits only).

ncbi_function: CSeq_id::Set raw route: general database tags with ':'
branch: all (UseDataLoaders; no tag, accession type e_not_set): text before the first ':' upper-cased and looked up (case-sensitively) in {ATGC BCMHGSC BERKELEY CELERA GSDB HOOD LANLCHGS LRG MIPS NCBI_EXT_ACC NCBI_GENOMES NCBI_MITO PGEC PID SGD SHGC SRA TIGR UOKNOR UWGC WASHU WIBR WUGSC dbGSS dbSTS}: found -> general Seq-id
notes: `SRA:SRR000001` is a Seq-id (general|SRA|SRR000001); the entries `dbGSS` and `dbSTS` contain lower-case letters and the key is upper-cased before the lookup, so they can never match (source quirk, `DBGSS:x` is FASTA). The rule is evaluated after IdentifyAccession returned no type.

ncbi_function: CSeq_id::Set raw route: local ID, retry, Malformatted ID
branch: all (UseDataLoaders): not a tag/accession/general: with fParse_ValidLocal and a valid local ID (non-blank, <=50 bytes, no byte in ` >[]|"`, no control or non-ASCII byte) -> local Seq-id, then `id->IsLocal() && !StartsWith(line, "lcl|")` -> retry CSeq_id(line) with default flags, which throws `Malformatted ID <line>` (CSeqIdException); an invalid local ID throws the same; ReadOneSeq catches it (message contains `Malformatted ID`) and falls back to CFastaReader
notes: Every line that is neither a known tag, an accession shape, nor a whitelisted `DB:` ends here and is read as FASTA data: `ACGTACGT`, a 40-nt line, `MKVLAAGIVGLLLAQ` (net4), `0123`, `ACGT ACGT`, a sequence-only file (record named Query_1, empty title; n01 outfmt 6 `Query_1`; net5 40-nt line -> Query_1). This is the common case that LOSAT rejects today (`unreadable_fasta`) and must read as FASTA with fDLOptional. A `lcl|...` line stays a Seq-id (tag route, no retry).

branch: all (UseDataLoaders): catch CSeqIdException containing `Malformatted ID` -> FASTA; any other CSeqIdException or std::exception -> rethrow; catch(...) -> FASTA
notes: Rethrown exceptions leave the reader with the line already consumed (no UngetLine): in GetNextSeqBatch they are swallowed (the next record starts at the following line), in GetAllSeqs (subject) they reach CATCH_ALL. Non-std exceptions (`...`) are the only other FASTA fallback (unreachable in practice).

branch: all (queries): while (size_read < GetBatchSize()) { if End() break; try q = GetNextSequence(scope) catch CObjReaderParseException: eEOF -> break, other codes -> rethrow; catch (const exception&) -> continue (SB-2307); size_read += GetLength(whole sequence); AddQuery } (lines 140-171; see rows 50-52 for the three catch branches)
notes: Batch sizes agree with LOSAT (query_batch.rs) but NCBI READS one batch at a time and the reader's side effects (stderr warnings, errors, Seq-id lookups, ID counter) happen at that moment. (1) A record without residues adds 0 to size_read, so it never closes a batch. (2) eEOF (only comments/blank lines left, `CFastaReader: Expected defline around line N`) ends the batch silently: a file with only comments/blank lines gives an empty batch and `BLAST engine error: Empty CBlastQueryVector` exit 3 after the outfmt 0 prolog (t03; outfmt 7: nothing on stdout, t04). (3) Any other CObjReaderParseException (`CFastaReader: Near line N, there's a line that doesn't look like plausible data, but it's not marked as defline or comment.`) is rethrown, reaches CATCH_ALL: `BLAST query error: <msg>` exit 1 AFTER the reports of the earlier batches were written and flushed, with no epilog (bb1: default blastn, 8 x 1000 nt, bad record 6: queries 1-5 reported, then the error; BATCH_SIZE=300: b_q_b2_bad_7 prints q1's rows then the error, no `# BLAST processed`; tblastx batch 10002: nothing printed because record 6 is in batch 1). (4) Every other exception (a Seq-id that is not found / not the molecule type / a CSeqIdException of the tag path, and the CInputException of a -query_loc that does not fit the record) is swallowed: the record is skipped without a message, its line(s) are consumed, and the loop re-tests End(); a skipped FASTA record used up its Query_<n>, a skipped Seq-id line did not (generator not advanced). (5) If the skipped records are the last ones, the NEXT batch is empty: Empty CBlastQueryVector exit 3 after the earlier batch's report (Nbd1/Lbd1: BATCH_SIZE=300, 300-nt q1 then a 3-nt record with -query_loc 5-100; LOSAT identical; the Seq-id variant follows from the same code). (6) size_read adds the length of the WHOLE sequence in the scope, not of the -query_loc range. Timing of reader warnings: row 47. LOSAT reads and checks the whole query file before searching (L08, L09, L10: its own reject text, nothing printed). After the port the queries must be read lazily per batch (BLASTX's FastaStream/parse_fasta_stream_with_warnings model) so that error timing, flushed output, skipped records and exit codes match.

branch: all (subjects): while (!End()) { try AddQuery(GetNextSequence) catch CObjReaderParseException: eEOF -> break; eNoDefline -> CInputException(`Query input doesn't start with a defline or comment, line <pos>` + trailing NUL); else rethrow }; no skip-on-error
notes: All subjects are read at once in the first handler. A reader error is fatal (`BLAST query error: ...` exit 1, o1), eEOF just ends the set, no exception is swallowed (a failed Seq-id lookup is fatal: net6). eNoDefline is reachable only with -parse_deflines (pd2). An empty set -> `Empty CBlastQueryVector` (see the -subject row).
